title: Any logged-in user can rewrite the content of any support-ticket comment (including staff/owner-internal ones) via a ticket they own
scenario: An ordinary user edits comments on other users' support tickets to tamper with support history or impersonate staff.
evidence: bob creates ticket #304 with comment #501 ('BOB-ORIGINAL'); alice creates her own ticket #<alice>; alice PATCH /api/tickets/<alice-ticket>/comments/501 {content:'HACKED'} → 200 {"success":true}; bob GET /api/tickets/304 shows comment #501 content = 'HACKED'
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nutzer manipuliert fremde Support-Ticket-Kommentare › a user cannot edit a comment on another user's ticket
cause: server/routes/tickets.ts:245-267 only verifies the caller can see ticket :id (getTicketById, which any user passes for their own ticket) and never checks that :cId belongs to :id or that the caller authored it. server/services/ticket-service.ts:209-213 editComment ignores _authorId/_userRole, and server/storage/support-storage.ts:253-265 updateComment updates by id with only an is_system=0 guard — so any non-system comment (internal owner-only ones included) can be rewritten by comment id.
fix: In editComment verify the comment's ticketId === the route :id AND (authorId === caller OR caller is owner); add `AND ticket_id = ? AND author_id = ?` (or an explicit role check) to updateComment and return 403/404 when no row matched.

title: Any logged-in user can delete any support-ticket comment via a ticket they own (IDOR)
scenario: An ordinary user deletes comments on other users' support tickets to destroy evidence or staff replies.
evidence: alice DELETE /api/tickets/<alice-ticket>/comments/501 (bob's comment) → 204; bob's ticket #304 no longer shows comment #501
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nutzer manipuliert fremde Support-Ticket-Kommentare › a user cannot delete a comment on another user's ticket
cause: server/routes/tickets.ts:270-288 gates only on getTicketById(:id); server/services/ticket-service.ts:216-219 deleteComment ignores _authorId/_userRole; server/storage/support-storage.ts:267-279 soft-deletes by id with only an is_system=0 guard, no author or ticket-linkage check.
fix: Verify the comment belongs to ticket :id and the caller authored it (or is owner) before deleting; add the matching WHERE clauses and 403/404 on no-match.

title: Non-member can read posts of a private community (feed filter and single-post view)
scenario: A logged-in user who is not a member reads the content of a private community.
evidence:
owner creates private community #348 and post #

inside it; non-member alice GET /api/posts?communityId=348 → 200 [ {post #

, content 'PRIV-SECRET'} ]; GET /api/posts/

→ 200 with full post
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nicht-Mitglied liest Inhalte einer privaten Community › a non-member cannot list posts of a private community via the feed filter / a non-member cannot read a single post of a private community
cause: server/storage/content-storage.ts getPosts() filters by community_id only — no privacy/membership check; server/routes/posts.ts:163-225 (GET /:id) and :227-285 (GET /) never check community visibility. The helpers server/utils/community-access.ts (canViewCommunity / hiddenCommunityIds) exist for exactly this but are not imported by any route.
fix: Apply canViewCommunity(req.user, post.communityId) in GET /api/posts/:id, and filter the list in GET /api/posts (and the communityId query path) with hiddenCommunityIds(req.user).

title: Shadow-banned user's comments leak through GET /api/posts/:postId/comments
scenario: A shadow-banned user's comments stay visible to other users, defeating the shadow-ban.
evidence:
shadow user comments 'SHADOW-COMMENT' on post #

, then owner shadow-bans them; viewer GET /api/posts/

omits the comment (correct) but GET /api/posts/

/comments → 200 [ {content:'SHADOW-COMMENT'} ]
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Shadowban-Umgehung – fremde Nutzer sehen verborgene Inhalte › the comments endpoint must hide a shadow-banned user's comment
cause: server/routes/posts.ts:424-445 returns all comments with no shadow-ban filtering, unlike the single-post view at server/routes/posts.ts:193 which drops comments whose author isShadowBanned.
fix: Apply the same shadow-ban filter used in GET /api/posts/:id (hide comments whose author isShadowBanned, except for the author themselves / other shadow-banned viewers) in GET /api/posts/:postId/comments.

title: Shadow-banned user's posts leak through their public profile (GET /api/:username/posts)
scenario: A shadow-banned user's posts stay visible on their profile to other users, defeating the shadow-ban that the main feed enforces.
evidence: shadow user posts 'shadow-post', then is shadow-banned; viewer GET /api/posts (feed) omits it (correct) but GET /api/<shadowuser>/posts → 200 [ {content:'shadow-post'} ]
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Shadowban-Umgehung – fremde Nutzer sehen verborgene Inhalte › a shadow-banned user's posts must not surface on their public profile
cause: server/routes/users.ts:110-150 (GET /:username/posts) returns the author's posts with no shadow-ban filter, whereas server/routes/posts.ts:267-278 filters shadow-banned authors out of the feed for other viewers.
fix: Hide a shadow-banned user's posts from other viewers on the profile endpoints as well (reuse the feed's isShadowBanned check), letting the author and other shadow-banned viewers still see them.

title: Admin with no permissions escalates to all permissions by creating an admin group and assigning it to themselves
scenario: An admin in no group creates an all-permissions group and assigns it to themselves to gain full admin rights.
evidence: adminNone GET /api/admin/settings → 403; POST /api/admin/groups {permissions:all} → 201; POST /api/admin/groups/assign {userId:self} → 200; after re-login GET /api/admin/settings → 200
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Admin ohne jede Berechtigung verschafft sich alle Rechte › an admin without the 'groups' permission cannot create an admin group / admin-without-permission → create group → assign self → read settings is blocked somewhere in the chain
cause: server/routes/admin-groups.ts:12,22,47,68,89 guard with isAdmin (role only); the 'groups' permission the UI uses is never checked.
fix: Guard admin-groups routes with hasPermission("groups"); forbid self-assignment and granting permissions the caller lacks.

title: Admin with only the 'users' permission escalates to all permissions by editing their own adminGroupId
scenario: An admin whose group only grants 'users' puts themselves into the all-permissions group via the user-edit route.
evidence: adminUsers GET /api/admin/settings → 403; PATCH /api/admin/users/<self> {adminGroupId:<all group>} → 200; after re-login GET /api/admin/settings → 200
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Admin mit nur 'users' eskaliert zu allen Rechten › the 'users' permission must not let an admin put themselves in another group
cause: server/routes/admin.ts:137-205 validates with adminUpdateUserSchema (shared/schema.ts:545) which includes adminGroupId/role/karma; nothing stops an admin editing their own adminGroupId.
fix: Remove privilege fields (adminGroupId/role) from adminUpdateUserSchema or require hasPermission("groups"); reject edits of the caller's own role/adminGroupId.

title: A non-owner admin can demote or lock out a platform owner
scenario: An admin changes an owner's role to admin or sets negative karma to invalidate the owner's session and block login.
evidence: adminAll PATCH /api/admin/users/<ownerB> {role:'admin'} → 200 (role becomes admin); {karma:-1} → 200 (karma<0 blocks the owner's login)
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Admin entmachtet oder sperrt einen Owner aus › an admin cannot demote a platform owner / an admin cannot lock an owner out via negative karma
cause: server/routes/admin.ts:159-186 only blocks promotion TO owner and demoting the LAST owner; any other change to an owner account by a non-owner admin is accepted.
fix: If the target's role is 'owner' and the caller is not an owner, reject any change (403), mirroring the DELETE rule at admin.ts:240.

title: Notifications expose the acting user's email and bcrypt password hash
scenario: Any user who receives a notification reads the actor's full user row, including email and password hash.
evidence: carol follows bob; bob GET /api/notifications → [{…, actor:{id, username, email, password:'$2b$…', role, …}}] (actor object still contains email and password)
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nutzer liest und verändert fremde Benachrichtigungen › notifications do not expose the acting user's email or password hash
cause: server/storage/notification-storage.ts (Postgres path) selects the full `actor: users` row and returns it unprojected.
fix: Project the actor to { id, username, profilePictureUrl } (as the SQLite path does) or run it through sanitizeUser / a public-user projection.

title: Any user can mark-as-read or delete (archive) other users' notifications (IDOR)
scenario: A user marks or archives notifications belonging to other users.
evidence: carol follows bob (bob gets a notification); alice POST /api/notifications/<bob's>/read → bob's notification now read; alice DELETE /api/notifications/<bob's> → notification archived out of bob's list
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nutzer liest und verändert fremde Benachrichtigungen › a user cannot mark another user's notification as read / a user cannot delete another user's notification
cause: server/routes/notifications.ts:76-104 never compares the notification's userId with req.user.id; storage.markNotificationAsRead / deleteNotification (server/storage/notification-storage.ts) update by id only.
fix: Scope the UPDATE to the caller (AND user_id = req.user.id) and return 404 when no row matched.

title: Member list of a private community is visible to any logged-in non-member
scenario: A non-member enumerates the members (ids, roles) of a private community.
evidence: non-member alice GET /api/communities/<private>/members → 200 with member list (user ids, roles)
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Nicht-Mitglied liest Inhalte einer privaten Community › a non-member cannot read the member list of a private community
cause: server/routes/communities.ts:477-486 only requires isAuthenticated and never checks community.isPrivate or membership.
fix: For private communities require membership (or global staff) before returning members (use canViewCommunity).

title: The 'tickets' permission is not enforced: every admin reads ticket stats and other users' tickets
scenario: An admin without the 'tickets' permission reads support ticket statistics and arbitrary users' tickets.
evidence: adminNone (no group) GET /api/tickets/stats → 200; GET /api/tickets/<bob's ticket> → 200 with full ticket, comments and history
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Admin ohne passende Berechtigung liest Moderationsdaten › an admin without 'tickets' cannot read ticket stats / an admin without 'tickets' cannot read another user's support ticket
cause: server/routes/tickets.ts:11-17,41 (checkAdminOrOwner = role only) and server/services/ticket-service.ts:30,89 grant access by role 'admin'; the UI requires the 'tickets' group permission.
fix: Check hasPermission("tickets") in checkAdminOrOwner and in TicketService.getTickets/getTicketById; an admin without it sees only their own tickets.

title: Admins can delete posts written by an owner (comments are protected, posts are not)
scenario: A non-owner admin deletes content authored by a platform owner.
evidence: adminNone (role admin) DELETE /api/posts/<post by owner> → 204; the equivalent DELETE /api/comments/:id on an owner's comment is correctly 403
test: tests/attacks/authz.attack.test.ts › Angriff: Admin löscht Inhalte eines Owners › an admin cannot delete a post written by an owner
cause: server/routes/posts.ts:287-300 allows any role 'admin'; server/utils/permissions.ts:11 (canDeleteContent, used for comments) excludes owner content — the two rules are inconsistent.
fix: Use canDeleteContent(req.user, post.authorId, author.role) in DELETE /api/posts/:id.
